newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis flatten ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis flatten ahead of data.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bonds largely flattened in early afternoon trade on Thursday as the market, having displayed decent but not exceptional demand for a surge in new issues, started bracing for Friday's economic data.

Retail sales as well as the producer prices will be released, and scrutinized as traders search for any signs that the economy might be growing rapidly, which could trigger the central bank to raise interest rates again.

The Producer Price Index for March was predicted at flat overall, though a rise of 0.1 percent was seen when the more volatile food and energy prices were excluded, economists said in a Reuters consensus survey.
Retail sales were seen gaining 0.6 percent overall, and 0.4 percent excluding autos.

This week's calender of new offerings rose to around $4.8 billion, the highest level seen this year, and renewed volatility in the stock market helped reawaken indidivual investors, who until recently spurned municipal bonds.
But retail buyers have not come roaring back, and this has made it more difficult for some dealers to keep their inventories in trim.

"We're higher than we'd like to be inventory-wise because only 60 percent of our normal retail is in," a trader said. But the trader added that this week has seen more demand from this sector than in the past few weeks.

Looking ahead to next week, traders questioned whether the Municipal Assistance Corporation (MAC) for New York City would match the strong showing seen in New York City's sale of $900 million of tax exempt bonds on Wednesday.
The MAC plans to sell $400 million of tax exempt bonds during the week of April 21, in a syndicate led by J.P. Morgan.

"I think it'll go well, but probably a little cheaper than last time," another trader said, explaining that in the previous sale, the new MAC bonds traded down a bit in the after market. "It's just on the back of your mind."

However, this concern was not matched by another trader, who noted his firm had sold those MAC bonds at a profit when two days after they were released to the after-market. "Since then, in the secondary market, I haven't really noticed any deterioration in price at all."

And while this week's deals went smoothly for a number of issuers, including New York City, the Clark County, Nev., School District, which had a $29 million balance left from a $300 million sale, and Massachusetts Water Pollution, which sold $137 million of debt, traders said the results were not outstanding.
"We're not sitting here cheering," one said.

In the secondary market, North Carolina Medical Care Commission Hospital revenue bonds for Wake County Hospital System of October 2026, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.93 percent, NET, up one basis point.
And Delaware River Port Authority of Pennyslvania and New Jersey revenue bonds of January 2026, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.87 percent, NET, also up one basis point.
In the futures market, the June municipal contract was flat at 112-7/32. The June Treasury bond contract fell five ticks to 107-6/32. The MOB spread was 161 ticks.
